note: Curated Microsoft Learn items and Saylor University courses. For each Microsoft Learn item the encoder proposed activities from the provider's title and summary; for each Saylor course the curator read the stated course learning outcomes. The curator kept only the links listed here (dwas), named the in-demand tools it teaches (tools, using O*NET software example names) and marked items that teach directing and checking AI output (ai_skill). Titles, URLs and durations come from the Microsoft Learn catalog API and from each Saylor course page when tools/build_catalogue.py runs. Route entries also record a coverage grade (introduces or practises), a practice checkpoint that produces an inspectable artifact and the entries they require first; Saylor states no prerequisites, so a requires link there is the curator's reading of the course sequence. families, where present, limits an entry to destination families in which its activities mean the same work (an activity such as "Test software performance" is unit testing for a developer but not for IT support). practice_access names a paid product the provider's own exercises need; the app then says the reading is free and the checkpoint works without it. focus names the units of a long course that serve the route. setup names what the practice checkpoint needs (software, accounts or materials), read from the checkpoint and the provider's stated prerequisites; a paid product the provider's own exercises use stays in practice_access.
